15:12.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ νεώτερος αὐτῶν τῷ πατρί Πάτερ, δός μοι τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος τῆς οὐσίας. ὁ δὲ διεῖλεν αὐτοῖς τὸν βίον.
15:12.targetText: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.

groups.note: The Greek articular comparative younger one is substantival and refers to the son; BSB expands it as The younger son. Son is contextual nominal support, not a separately printed Greek son noun.

Greek to the father is pronominalized as to him, referring to the same father addressed immediately afterward. The complete recipient noun phrase is retained rather than claiming father is lexically a personal pronoun.

The definite due/falling share phrase names the portion due to the requesting speaker. BSB condenses that nominal constituent to my share; the contextual first-person possession is not an isolated meaning of the falling/due participle.
The Greek dative to them names the division recipients; English expresses the same distributive role as between them.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB omits the Greek opening and at this verse boundary.
N1904 specifies of them with the younger one; BSB uses the younger son without separately expressing the sibling-set pronoun.
The article is not separately expressed with BSB his property.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB makes the property possessor explicit; N1904 has the definite property/living noun without a possessive pronoun.
